take.title: Take one of these back to your team
take.description: Nothing here is graded and nothing is checked. 4 of the 5 are things to work out rather than things to build, so the tick is a bookmark.
take.queue.label: Write down what stands between your work being finished and it reaching production, and cross off anything that is typing.
take.sentence.label: Write the line you will say at the next demo about what the rough version does not do yet.
take.line.label: Pick 1 correction you gave an agent more than 1 time this week and write it into the repository's own instruction file.
take.practice.label: Pick 1 ritual your team keeps, write down the constraint it was built for, and say whether that constraint is still there.
take.person.label: Put one of the first 4 in front of 1 person on your team. A name and a date.
pipeline-shift.description: The same 5 stages 2 times, drawn on one scale. Above, the way it ran when a person typed the code: deciding, waiting, a wide block of writing, verifying, releasing. Below, the way it runs with agents: writing is a sliver run as 3 lanes at once, verifying is the widest solid block, and both waiting stages are wider than they were. Under that second row, a dashed strip shows the verifying 3 lanes need. It runs well past the block above it, and a mark on it shows where the checking actually stopped.
pipeline-shift.caption: The times are illustrative. The scale is not: both rows are drawn against one clock, and the strip under the second is 3 lanes of output at what 1 lane cost to read.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.question: On Thursday you demo a working feature and everyone considers it 'done'. Three weeks later, however, you are still coding on it, with nothing waiting on a review or a release window. Where did those three weeks go?
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.cases: To unforeseen situations; edge cases that were overlooked while writing the question, or that only arose when the feature was already half done.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.vague: The scope was too vague; with a sharper question these edge cases would already have surfaced in the first run.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.poor: The agent's implementation was of low quality, so almost everything had to be redone by hand.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.queue: To automated testing; the demo ran on untested code that still needed tests.
quiz.three-weeks-after-thursday.explanat: An agent implements the request it was given, along the path you described. A sharper first draft does not produce the detail nobody knew about yet, so the burden moved rather than lifted.
quiz.their-prototype.question: During lunch, a manager put together a working prototype and shows it in the meeting. The code has no validation and uses a hard-coded user. What do you do?
quiz.their-prototype.say: You name what is still missing right away, out loud, in the meeting.
quiz.their-prototype.theirs: You say nothing; it is their prototype, so it is up to them to point out the caveats.
quiz.their-prototype.ticket: You record the missing parts in a ticket, so the decision makers can read them.
quiz.their-prototype.build: You first build a full version and then show what a finished product looks like.
quiz.their-prototype.explanation: What it does not do gets said either way. Left out now, it is said later by somebody asking why the feature they signed off on falls over on an empty list.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.question: Work that used to take a week was now done in a single afternoon. Your manager asks what output the team can commit to this quarter. What do you answer?
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.checkpoint: The next checkpoint and what will be done by then; after all, that one afternoon is only one data point.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.fourtimes: Four times the old output; after all, that afternoon shows the new pace.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.old: The original estimate; after all, one fast run says nothing about a whole quarter.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.average: The average of the last three runs; you will not get a more accurate indication of speed.
quiz.one-afternoon-quarter.explanation: Hand the same request over 2 times and it does not come back the same 2 times. 1 afternoon is a single reading of a job that has changed shape, too few to set a new rate on.
deck.change.test-engineer.title: You are <hi>the test engineer</hi> now
deck.change.test-engineer.note: Reading every line stops scaling. The case the agent did not think of does.
deck.change.business.title: Knowing the domain is <hi>not scope creep</hi>
deck.change.business.note: A version by Thursday only helps if somebody who knows what it was for looks at it on Thursday.
deck.change.pipelines.title: The process was <hi>the bottleneck</hi>
deck.change.rethink.title: The way of working is <hi>a decision</hi>
deck.change.rethink.2: Review, when <mute>an agent wrote the diff</mute>
deck.change.gates.title: Taste relaxes. <hi>The gates do not.</hi>
deck.change.environment.title: The deliverable is <hi>the environment</hi>, <mute>not this quarter</mute>
deck.change.environment.note: Count the times this week you told an agent something you had told it before. Each one is a line missing from a file.
deck.expectations.floor.title: A gain your competitor also gets is <hi>a floor</hi>, <mute>not a lead</mute>
deck.expectations.missing.title: Say what is missing <hi>when you show it</hi>
deck.expectations.missing.note: That sentence gets said either way. Later, and from a worse position.
deck.expectations.burden.title: The burden moved. <hi>It did not lift.</hi>
deck.expectations.burden.note: Finished Thursday, then 3 more weeks on the cases nobody could have written down.
deck.expectations.estimate.title: Say the date <hi>including the checking</hi>
deck.expectations.estimate.note: They got faster. Your reading did not. Otherwise "done" means 2 things in one room.
deck.expectations.velocity.title: 1 good run is not <hi>a velocity</hi>
deck.expectations.velocity.note: Promise the next checkpoint, not the finish.
deck.impostor.engineer.title: You are still <hi>the engineer</hi>
deck.impostor.engineer.note: The route was the agent's. The goal, the check and the reading were yours.
deck.impostor.signal.title: Tell the feeling from <hi>the signal</hi>
deck.impostor.signal.note: A diff you cannot follow is a gap with a fix.
deck.impostor.written.title: Nobody has been doing this <hi>long</hi>
deck.impostor.written.note: The tools changed 2 times while this course was written. A file that stopped needing the same correction is the only record of that.
deck.change.divider.1: Producing code is not the job
deck.change.divider.2: Business joins weekly, <mute>not at the demo</mute>
deck.change.divider.3: Typing was never what the calendar waited on
deck.expectations.divider.1: They saw an afternoon, <mute>and priced everything at one</mute>
deck.expectations.divider.2: The estimate still includes the checking
deck.expectations.divider.3: The burden moved. <mute>It did not lift.</mute>
deck.impostor.divider.1: It lands when the agent is <hi>good</hi>
deck.impostor.divider.3: What adds up is <hi>what you wrote down</hi>
